content: Start by reading TASK.md, then complete the assignment.

content.content:
1	# Task 2: forest of 10,000 instances
2	
3	Build a scene with three.js 0.185.1 (`three` and `@types/three`, already installed in node_modules).
4	
5	Requirements:
6	1. A ground plane and exactly 10,000 scattered objects drawn with instancing (not 10,000 separate meshes): 8,000 trees (a trunk and a canopy, each instanced) and 2,000 rocks.
7	2. Placement is deterministic from a fixed seed (same forest every load), no overlaps needed.
8	3. Per-instance colour variation (canopies and rocks do not all share one colour).
9	4. One directional light that casts shadows, and exponential fog.
10	5. The camera slowly orbits the forest and the whole scene is visible.
11	
12	The rendering contract in the next section applies.
13	
14	## Rendering contract (all tasks)
15	
16	- Draw into the existing `<canvas id="app">` (640x360 CSS pixels, device pixel ratio 1). Do not resize it or create another canvas.
17	- Render continuously with `requestAnimationFrame`. When the first frame has been drawn set `window.__EVAL_READY__ = true`.
18	- No network access: load assets only from `/assets/...` (served from `public/assets`). Do not import from CDNs.
19	- Code goes in `src/` (TypeScript, strict). The entry is `src/main.ts`. It must pass `typecheck` and build with `vite build`.
20	- When you are done, call `finish`.
21

content.thinking:
I need a type declaration for window.__EVAL_READY__. For the scene design, I'm planning a forest with radius around 60, a ground plane of 160, and exponential fog matching the background color so everything stays visible. The camera orbits at radius 90 and height 45 looking at center, with a directional light casting shadows covering ±60 at 2048 map size, and instanced meshes set to cast and receive shadows.

I'm working out tree density and placement using per-instance colors, cone canopies, and cylinder trunks—around 8000 trees over a disk radius of 55 with varied scale. I'm tuning camera distance, fov, and fog density numerically so the forest reads clearly without being obscured, settling on fog density near 0.0035 for about 88% visibility at distance 100. I'm also adding seeded random rocks using flattened dodecahedron geometry with HSL coloring, and a ground circle radius 80 that receives shadows while fog masks the horizon.

Setting up canopy hue range, directional light shadow bounds and bias, and a ready flag triggered after the first render frame, plus configuring the renderer to a fixed 640x360 size at pixel ratio 1.
The camera orbit is driven by elapsed time so the initial frame stays roughly deterministic, which works fine here.

input.summary: I wrote src/main.ts. It builds a forest of 8,000 trees and 2,000 rocks. Trunks, canopies and rocks are each one InstancedMesh, so there are three draw calls for the 10,000 objects. Placement uses a seeded mulberry32 generator, so the forest is the same on every load. Canopy, trunk and rock colours vary per instance through instanceColor. There is one shadow-casting directional light plus a hemisphere fill light. The scene has FogExp2 and a ground disc. The camera orbits slowly at radius 92 and height 58, looking at the centre, so the whole forest stays in view. `window.__EVAL_READY__` is set after the first frame renders. `typecheck` passes. I did not run `vite build` or open the page in a browser, so I haven't seen how it renders.
